entries.note: Minimal utility and minimal value express an appraisal without an agreed standard. The extracted proposition excludes the separate prediction about a transient fad.

entries.test: If generative AI proves useful, public infrastructure arrangements, contracts, and payment records would show whether a handful of established tech companies collect a cut from every LLM-based app and service.
entries.note: The preceding sentence explicitly supplies the condition that the technology becomes useful. The universal claim about collecting a cut is testable despite the pejorative wording.

entries.test: Contemporaneous financial reporting, documented commercial results, and market evidence would show whether generative AI's losses and inadequate problem-solving returns prevented the described oligopoly from succeeding.
entries.note: “I don’t think” introduces his asserted assessment rather than an explicit probability. The surrounding discussion identifies the proposed oligopoly as control of commercially useful models and their revenues.

entries.test: Public evidence of the described AI monopoly strategy failing while its models delivered adequate business returns would refute the claim that inadequate returns are its only failure condition.
entries.note: “Only” asserts a necessary condition, leaving the claim open to counterexamples involving other causes of failure.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures establishing generative AI as a sustained source of additional growth for big tech would refute the claim.
entries.note: The claim concerns generative AI's capacity to sustain future growth. The separate “may not” statement about Meta and Google's survival does not hedge this assertion.
